skill.name: changelog
skill.description: Maintains the IdeaVim changelog by reviewing releases, commits, and pull requests, then organizing user-focused entries in CHANGES.md.
skill.summary: Reviews IdeaVim changes and maintains clear, correctly formatted changelog entries.
skill.author: JetBrains

security_audit.summary: All 54 static findings are false positives. The detected backticks are Markdown examples or command references, the URLs are documentation links, and the reconnaissance matches are ordinary editorial guidance; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Shell commands include placeholder values such as commit SHAs and pull request numbers.
remediation.suggestion: Validate placeholder values and pass them as separate arguments through a process API. Require confirmation before any command can modify repository state.

remediation.issue: The workflow directs the agent to inspect GitHub and other external documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep network access opt-in, restrict retrieval to the documented JetBrains and repository domains, and avoid sending local content to external services.

remediation.issue: The workflow can update CHANGES.md and create a pull request.
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only review by default and require explicit user approval before writing files, pushing changes, or opening a pull request.

content.value_statement: Release notes become inconsistent when commits, tickets, and user impact are reviewed separately. This skill turns repository history into organized, user-focused IdeaVim changelog entries.
actual_capabilities: Reviews the top portion of CHANGES.md and identifies the current unreleased section.
Inspects commits, tags, pull requests, and selected file changes for user-visible updates.
Groups entries into features, fixes, changes, and merged pull requests.
Preserves IdeaVim heading, ordering, linking, and historical-gap conventions.
Writes concise changelog descriptions with relevant issue and pull request references.
limitations: It cannot determine user impact when repository changes or tests lack sufficient detail.
It depends on available Git, GitHub CLI, repository, and network access.
It does not validate the final changelog against every project build or release rule.
It should not publish changes or create pull requests without explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Review changes since the last release and organize them into a clean, user-facing changelog draft.

use_cases.title: Document Merged Work
use_cases.description: Identify important features and fixes from commits and pull requests, then add accurate issue references.

use_cases.title: Review a Changelog Update
use_cases.description: Check an existing draft for duplicate entries, incorrect sections, missing context, and formatting problems.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Unreleased Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current repository changes and draft concise entries for the To Be Released section of CHANGES.md.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review commits since the previous version, identify user-visible changes, and group them into Features, Fixes, and Changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Entries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current changelog draft for duplicates, vague descriptions, incorrect ticket placement, and violations of the IdeaVim format.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile History and Pull Requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare tags, commits, merged pull requests, tests, and recent changelog updates. Produce a release-ready draft and explain each inclusion or exclusion.

output_examples.input: Review the latest changes and draft the unreleased changelog entries.
output: ### Features: Added support for the gn text object and Next Edit Suggestion integration.
### Fixes: Fixed ci" behavior in empty strings and cursor positioning after undo.

output_examples.input: Check this release draft for quality and repository conventions.
output: Moved the ticket link before the fix description.
Removed a duplicate entry and clarified the affected Vim command.

best_practices: Describe visible behavior and user impact instead of internal implementation details.
Review tests and actual file changes before writing a specific entry.
Preserve the existing structure, newest-first order, and exact release headings.
anti_patterns: Do not invent issue numbers, release dates, or behavior not supported by repository evidence.
Do not duplicate one change across multiple changelog sections.
Do not edit build configuration or create a pull request without explicit approval.

faq.question: What file does this skill maintain?
faq.answer: It maintains the IdeaVim CHANGES.md file and focuses on its top section and recent releases.

faq.question: What sources does it review?
faq.answer: It reviews changelog content, commits, tags, pull requests, issue references, tests, and relevant file changes.

faq.question: How does it choose entries?
faq.answer: It prioritizes user-visible features, fixes, breaking changes, deprecations, and significant external contributions.

faq.question: Does it include internal refactoring?
faq.answer: It excludes internal work unless it has clear user impact or qualifies under the merged pull request rules.

faq.question: Can it create a pull request?
faq.answer: The workflow describes pull request creation, but users should require explicit approval before any repository mutation.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
